headline: A key whose private key anyone can recover is refused wherever the framework signs, verifies or trusts with it, and every TLS peer's certificate chain is checked up to a trust anchor
summary:
Some keys in circulation have a private half anyone can obtain: CA and interception roots whose private keys were published (the eMudhra CA keys, Superfish and the other Komodia roots, PrivDog, the Adguard CA keys, eDellRoot, DSDTestProvider, the bealocalhost.de root and the PKfail Secure Boot platform key), and elliptic-curve keys whose private scalar is so small that the public key gives it away. The new `b.crypto.compromisedKey(key)` reports both: one of the 36 keys the vendored `@blamejs/pki` 0.9.7 lists, or a P-256, P-384, P-521 or secp256k1 key whose private scalar is below 256 or within 255 of the group order. Every primitive that signs with a key, verifies with one, or trusts a certificate now refuses such a key with its own `<module>/compromised-key` code. No option turns the check off for signing and verification. A TLS client set to `rejectUnauthorized: false` (or `allowInsecure` on the OTLP/gRPC log stream) still connects after the check refuses the server's chain, as it does after any other verification failure.

Every framework TLS client now walks the certificate chain the server sends from the leaf to a trust anchor of the connection and refuses a compromised key on that path or in the anchor with `tls/compromised-key`. A chain that reaches no anchor is refused with the new code `tls/server-chain-unverifiable`. `b.router`, `b.createApp` and the new `b.network.tls.checkClientChains(server)` apply the same walk to client certificates. On Node 24 a listener sees only the client's leaf, so the CA certificates that issue client certificates must be listed in the listener's `ca`.

node's `X509Certificate` reads a PEM block embedded in DER bytes ahead of the DER around it. A leaf issued under a compromised intermediate could carry the trust root's PEM in an extension and pass the TLS chain check as the root itself, and an S/MIME, DANE, OID4VCI or mTLS revocation check could judge one certificate and trust another. Every certificate the framework builds from bytes is now read as the DER it is.

Several changes refuse input that was accepted before. The Migration section lists what to change. The public suffix list is the 2026-10-22_08-36-41_UTC edition.

items.title: Keys whose private key is public are refused
items.body:
`b.crypto.compromisedKey(key)` returns `null` for an ordinary key and a frozen `{ id, reason }` otherwise, with `id` `"listed"` for a published key and `"small-ec-scalar"` for an EC key whose private scalar is below 256 or within 255 of the group order. It reads a `KeyObject`, a WebCrypto `CryptoKey`, an `X509Certificate`, PEM text (every certificate under the `CERTIFICATE`, `X509 CERTIFICATE` and `TRUSTED CERTIFICATE` labels and every key block), a DER certificate or SubjectPublicKeyInfo, and a public JWK. A listed key matches however it is encoded. `b.crypto.assertNotCompromised(key, opts?)` throws instead.

`b.crypto.sign` throws `crypto/compromised-key` and `b.crypto.verify` returns `false` for such a key. The same check refuses a compromised signing, verification, issuer, holder, anchor or chain key in `b.mtlsCa` (`mtls-ca/compromised-key`), `b.x509Chain`, `b.acme` and `b.cert`, `b.cose`, `b.cwt`, `b.eat`, `b.scitt`, `b.vc`, `b.did`, `b.auth.jwt.verifyExternal`, `b.auth.jar`, `b.auth.jws`, `b.auth.oauth` (ID tokens, JARM, back-channel logout tokens, client attestations), `b.auth.ciba`, `b.auth.dpop` and `b.middleware.dpop`, `b.auth.sdJwtVc`, `b.auth.oid4vci`, `b.auth.oid4vp`, `b.auth.openidFederation`, `b.auth.saml`, `b.auth.passkey`, `b.auth.fidoMds3`, `b.breakGlass`, `b.dbsc`, `b.middleware.protectedResourceMetadata`, `b.mail.dkim`, `b.mail.arc`, `b.mail.crypto.pgp`, `b.mail.crypto.smime`, `b.mail.bimi`, `b.mail.deploy.danePublish`, `b.network.dns.dane`, `b.network.smtp.policy.dane`, `b.network.dns.dnssec`, `b.tsa`, `b.mdoc`, `b.contentCredentials`, `b.privacyPass`, `b.a2a`, `b.ai.modelManifest`, `b.compliance.aiAct.gpai`, `b.auditSign`, `b.agent.snapshot`, `b.mcp` tool registries, `b.selfUpdate` and `b.selfUpdate.standaloneVerifier`. A verifier that returns a result instead of throwing reports `reason: "compromised-key"`, `valid: false` or a `compromised-key` entry in its errors.

A `ca` given to `b.network.dns.useDnsOverHttps`, `useDnsOverTls`, `b.network.ntp.nts.performKeHandshake`, the Redis clients behind `b.cache`, `b.pubsub`, `b.websocketChannels` and `b.queue`, the syslog and OTLP/gRPC log streams, `b.mail.transports.smtp` and `b.router` `tlsOptions` throws its module's `compromised-key` code when it holds a compromised certificate, and a `BLAMEJS_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` file or `BLAMEJS_EXTRA_CA_CERTS_DIR` directory holding one makes `b.network.bootFromEnv` throw `tls/compromised-key`. `b.network.tls.useSystemTrust(true)` adds the system roots without the ones whose key is compromised. Without a `ca`, a certificate in Node's default store whose key is compromised (one added through `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `--use-system-ca` or `tls.setDefaultCACertificates`) is left out of the trust used by framework dials and listeners.

items.title: TLS clients check the server's chain up to a trust anchor
items.body:
`b.httpClient` (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, a `b.network.proxy` tunnel and an `opts.agent`), `b.network.tls.applyToContext` with role client, `b.network.tls.buildOptions`, `ocsp.connect`, `connectWithEch`, `b.pqcAgent`, `b.wsClient`, the SMTP transport, DNS over HTTPS and TLS, `b.network.dns.resolver`, NTS-KE, Redis and the syslog and OTLP/gRPC log streams walk the chain the server sends from the leaf to the first certificate that is a trust anchor of the dial, or that such an anchor signed. The anchors are the dial's `ca`, or Node's default store when the dial sets none, matched by certificate or by subject and public key. A compromised key on that path or in the anchor fails with `tls/compromised-key`. A chain that reaches no anchor, or that has an expired certificate or a broken signature before it reaches one, fails with `tls/server-chain-unverifiable`. In the DNS, resolver, NTS, Redis, OTLP/gRPC and SMTP clients a compromised key fails with `dns/compromised-key`, `resolver/compromised-key`, `nts/compromised-key`, `redis-client/compromised-key`, `log-stream-otlp-grpc/compromised-key` and `mail/compromised-key`, and a chain that reaches no anchor fails under their usual codes (`dns/doh-failed`, `dns/dot-handshake-failed`, `resolver/upstream-failed`, `nts/ke-socket`, `redis-client/connect`, `log-stream-otlp-grpc/http2-error`, `mail/smtp-failed`). The syslog stream drops the connection and reconnects.

Issuer and subject names compare as X.509 names, so a name that differs from the anchor's only in case or repeated spaces still reaches it. An anchor may issue without basicConstraints `cA:TRUE` when OpenSSL accepts it as an issuer: a self-signed X.509 v1 root, or a root with keyUsage `keyCertSign` and no basicConstraints. A dial whose trust the check cannot read (a prebuilt `secureContext` without a `ca` the framework built it from, or a `pfx` whose CA certificates Node trusts) is walked the same way, and a chain that reaches no anchor the check knows is then checked certificate by certificate as Node shows it: each one for a compromised key and for a signature by the certificate shown as its issuer. A `b.httpClient` `opts.agent` that sets its own `checkServerIdentity` has that option replaced, on first use, by a function that runs the chain check and then the agent's function.

A server that placed an expired alternate issuer and a self-signed decoy root ahead of a path through a compromised CA passed the earlier check, which accepted any chain ending in a self-signed certificate. That chain is now refused. An expired cross-certificate that carries a trusted root's name and key, a chain that leaves out the root, and a leaf a trusted root issued directly keep working.

The check reads its anchors from the `ca` of the dial it runs on, so a `checkServerIdentity` from `applyToContext` or `buildOptions` can be reused on a dial with another `ca`. A dial that passes a prebuilt `secureContext` is checked against the `ca` the options were built with. Node does not run `checkServerIdentity` on a resumed session, so a `rejectUnauthorized: false` dial that resumes the session of a connection the check refused reports `authorized: true`. An `https.Agent` drops the session of a connection that closed with an error, so a dial through one that keeps verification on is refused each time. Under `--use-openssl-ca`, the anchors are the default store, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR` and, on Linux, `tls.getCACertificates("system")`; a compromised certificate in `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` no longer makes those dials replace the OpenSSL store.

items.title: TLS listeners check client chains
items.body: `b.network.tls.checkClientChains(server)` checks the chain of every client a `tls.Server`, `https.Server` or HTTP/2 secure server authorizes, against the listener's `ca` (Node's default store without one). A chain carrying a compromised key sets `socket.authorized` to `false` with `authorizationError` `tls/compromised-key`. A chain that reaches no anchor sets `tls/client-chain-unverifiable`, or `tls/resumed-chain-unverifiable` on a resumed session. Each refusal writes the audit row `tls.client_chain.refused` and closes the socket unless `rejectUnauthorized` is `false`. The listener sets `SSL_OP_NO_TICKET`, so a client cannot resume a session from a ticket and sends its chain on a full handshake. A listener whose trust the check cannot read (one built with a `pfx`, or serving other secure contexts through `SNICallback` or `addContext`) checks a chain that reaches no anchor in its `ca` certificate by certificate as Node shows it. `b.router` and `b.createApp` listeners with `tlsOptions.requestCert` run the same check, and `b.middleware.requireMtls` and `b.middleware.requireBoundKey` refuse with reasons `compromised-key`, `client-chain-unverifiable` and `resumed-chain-unverifiable`. The result is kept per socket and leaf certificate, so keep-alive requests do not walk the chain again. `requireBoundKey` judges a `req.peerCert` forwarded by a TLS-terminating proxy by the chain its `issuerCertificate` links carry.

items.title: A DER certificate is read as the certificate it encodes
items.body: node's `new X509Certificate(buffer)` reads a `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` block embedded anywhere in the bytes ahead of the DER around it. A leaf issued under a compromised intermediate that carried the trust root's PEM text in an extension was matched by the TLS chain check as the root itself, and the dial connected. `b.middleware.requireMtls` looked up the embedded certificate's serial in `revocationSource.isSerialRevoked`, so a revoked client certificate carrying another certificate's PEM passed. An OID4VCI proof `x5c`, a DANE or SMTP DANE match, an S/MIME `SignedData` chain, a TSA token, an mdoc `x5chain`, a FIDO MDS3 BLOB, a passkey attestation chain and its roots, `b.crypto.spkiPin` and `b.crypto.encryptEnvelopeAsCertPeer` could likewise judge or use the embedded certificate. Each now reads DER bytes as the certificate they encode, and `b.crypto.compromisedKey` throws `crypto/bad-key` for DER followed by extra bytes instead of reading PEM text inside it. An ordinary DER certificate that carries a `-----BEGIN` line no longer throws `crypto/bad-key`. A `req.peerCert` whose `raw` is not DER is refused by `requireMtls` and `requireBoundKey` with reason `compromised-key` when its key is compromised and `client-chain-unverifiable` otherwise. An EC key whose explicit curve parameters name no standard curve (its base point differs from the named curve's) throws `crypto/bad-key` from `b.crypto.compromisedKey`, so every check that uses it refuses the key.

items.title: A certificate `@blamejs/pki` cannot parse is judged by its key
items.body: `b.crypto.compromisedKey` judges a certificate by the key node loads from it as well as by the `@blamejs/pki` key-compromise lint. A certificate whose extension encodes its critical flag as an explicit `FALSE`, which `@blamejs/pki` refuses to parse, was reported as clean, so `b.tsa.verifyToken`, `b.mdoc.verifyIssuerSigned`, `b.contentCredentials`, `b.auth.fidoMds3.fetch` and `b.x509Chain` trusted a scalar-1 key in one. `crypto/bad-key` is thrown only when neither node nor the lint can read the certificate. `b.x509Chain.resolveChain` and `issuerValidlyIssued` treat a certificate whose key cannot be checked as unusable; the refusal reads `certificate '<subject>' could not be checked for a compromised key: <detail>`.

items.title: Passkey attestations and stored credentials
items.body: `b.auth.passkey.verifyRegistration` throws `auth-passkey/compromised-key` when the credential public key, any certificate of the attestation `x5c` chain (packed, tpm, android-key, apple, fido-u2f and the android-safetynet JWS chain), or any `attestationRoots` or `safetyNetRoots` certificate carries a compromised key, whether or not a root is configured. An attestation chain of more than 10 certificates is refused with `auth-passkey/bad-att-stmt` before any certificate is read. `verifyAuthentication` throws `auth-passkey/compromised-key` for a stored credential whose key is compromised, and `b.breakGlass.grant` fails such a passkey factor with `breakglass/bad-factor`. `b.auth.fidoMds3.fetch` throws `fido-mds3/compromised-key` for a `caCertificate` or BLOB `x5c` certificate with a compromised key and `fido-mds3/bad-x5c` for an `x5c` chain over 10 certificates.

items.title: DKIM and ARC bind the key type to the algorithm
items.body: `b.mail.dkim.verify` and `b.mail.arc.verify` / `evaluate` require the selector key to be the type the `a=` tag names: RSA for `rsa-sha256`, Ed25519 for `ed25519-sha256`. Any other key, whatever `k=` says, is a permerror `DKIM key type <type> does not match a=<alg>`, and an ARC set using one is not trusted. The ARC-Seal applies the same 2048-bit RSA floor as DKIM and the ARC-Message-Signature, so a smaller sealer key fails with `too small`. A selector that publishes a compromised key fails before any signature check with `DKIM key is a compromised key: <reason>` or `as: key is a compromised key: <reason>`.

items.title: Content Credentials identity assertions are bound to the leaf certificate
items.body: `b.contentCredentials.verifyIdentityAssertion` reports `verified: true` for an x509 identity only when the leaf certificate carries the key that signed the assertion (otherwise `reason: "leaf-key-mismatch"`) and every signed subject field (name, org, orgUnit, country, locality, state, id) equals the matching attribute (CN, O, OU, C, L, ST, serialNumber) of the leaf's subject (otherwise `reason: "subject-not-certified"`). A compromised chain certificate or issuing anchor returns `reason: "compromised-key"` ahead of `leaf-expired`, `chain-cert-expired` and `broken-chain`, and a chain certificate whose key cannot be checked returns `bad-chain-cert`. An unrelated compromised certificate in the trust-anchor list no longer makes a valid chain unverified.

items.title: Configuration baselines and agent snapshots trust only the live signing key
items.body: `b.configDrift` detectors verify the baseline sidecar only under the live `b.auditSign` key. A sidecar signed by any other key, including a rotated-out key listed in the unsealed `audit-sign.pubkeys.json`, is reported by `checkpoint()` and `read()` as tampered with reason `signer-untrusted`, and both throw `audit-sign/not-initialized` before `b.auditSign.init()`. `b.agent.snapshot` handles without `opts.signer` verify a stored snapshot only under the live key and throw `agent-snapshot/bad-signature` otherwise. A handle whose `opts.signer` reports a key from `getPublicKey()` passes that current key to `signer.verify`, not the `sigPubKey` stored with the row, so a row signed by another key under its own `sigPubKey` is refused. When that signer's `getPublicKey()` throws or returns a key `b.crypto.compromisedKey` cannot read, such as a KMS key name, `loadLatest`, `loadById` and `resign` throw `agent-snapshot/signer-key-unreadable`; when it returns a compromised key, they throw `agent-snapshot/compromised-key`. They judge a stored `sigPubKey` in every form (PEM text, base64 SPKI DER, a Buffer or its JSON form, a JWK) and refuse a compromised or unreadable one. A row without a sealed wrapper is refused with `agent-snapshot/plaintext-refused` unless `allowPlaintext` is set. `persist()` throws `agent-snapshot/compromised-key` or `agent-snapshot/signer-key-unreadable` for an operator signer whose `getPublicKey()` returns a compromised or unreadable key, and writes nothing.

items.title: `b.crypto.spkiPinVerifier` checks the chain before the pin
items.body: The verifier walks the server's chain to a trust anchor of the dial before it checks identity and the pin, so a pinned leaf under a compromised CA, or behind an expired alternate issuer and a decoy root, is refused with `tls/compromised-key` or `tls/server-chain-unverifiable` even when the pin matches.

items.title: DANE and DNSSEC
items.body: `b.network.smtp.policy.dane.verifyChain` counts a PKIX-TA (usage 0) match only when a signature-verified path runs from the leaf to the pinned certificate (otherwise `pkix-ta-path-not-validated`), reports `dane-compromised-key` for a compromised leaf, matched anchor or certificate on the path, and reports `dane-unreadable-key` with `ok: false` for a match on bytes that carry no readable key. `b.mail.transports.smtp` counts a PKIX-TA or PKIX-EE match only when the handshake validated the relay's path, and refuses a relay whose TLSA match or chain carries a compromised key with `mail/compromised-key` before AUTH. `b.network.dns.dane.matchCertificate` throws `dane/compromised-key` for a compromised leaf, or when every trust-anchor match is compromised or reached only through a compromised certificate. `b.network.dns.dnssec.verifyRrset`, `verifyChain` and `verifyDs` throw `dnssec/compromised-key` for a compromised DNSKEY, and `verifyDs` throws `dnssec/ds-mismatch` when the DS algorithm differs from the DNSKEY algorithm.

items.title: The OpenID Federation chain audit row is written
items.body: `b.auth.openidFederation.buildTrustChain` writes its audit row as `auth.openid_federation.chain_built`. The previous action name was refused by `b.audit`, so no row was written.

items.title: DNS over HTTPS honors the environment proxy
items.body: `b.network.dns` DNS-over-HTTPS queries and the default transport of `b.network.dns.resolver` go through Node's environment proxy (`HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`) again when `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` or `--use-env-proxy` is set, with the chain check applied behind the CONNECT tunnel.

items.title: `b.httpClient` reuses proxy tunnels
items.body: Requests through `b.network.proxy` reuse their CONNECT tunnel and TLS connection again.

items.title: A published JWKS object is accepted
items.body: `b.auth.jwt.verifyExternal` and `b.auth.jar.parse` accept `opts.jwks` as the published JWKS object `{ keys: [...] }` as well as an array of JWKs. Any other shape throws `auth-jwt-external/bad-jwks`.

items.title: Fetch failures carry the module's code
items.body: The default fetcher of `b.auth.openidFederation.buildTrustChain` and `resolveLeaf` throws `auth-openid-federation/fetch-failed` for a reply outside 2xx (it threw `http-client/http-error`) and `auth-openid-federation/empty-response` for an empty 2xx body (it threw `auth-openid-federation/bad-statement`). `b.auth.jwt.verifyExternal` throws `auth-jwt-external/jwks-fetch-failed` when the `jwksUri` reply is outside 2xx.

items.title: Unknown mail crypto options carry a code
items.body: `b.mail.crypto.pgp.sign`, `verify`, `experimental.encrypt` and `experimental.decrypt` throw `mail-crypto/pgp/bad-opts`, and `b.mail.crypto.smime.sign`, `verify`, `verifyAll` and `checkCert` throw `mail-crypto/smime/bad-opts`, for an unknown option. Each threw a plain `Error` with no code.

items.title: Composite ML-DSA certificates
items.body: `b.mail.crypto.smime.checkCert` checks a certificate whose key node cannot load, such as a composite ML-DSA key, with `b.crypto.compromisedKey` and returns it with `keyType: null`; it throws `mail-crypto/smime/bad-cert` only when neither can read the key, where a raw `ERR_OSSL_EVP_DECODE_ERROR` escaped before. `b.network.dns.dane.matchCertificate`, `b.network.smtp.policy.dane.verifyChain` and `b.mail.deploy.danePublish` with selector 1 hash the SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes the certificate carries when node cannot load its key, so such a certificate matches and publishes.

items.title: S/MIME chains compare issuer names as X.509 names
items.body: `b.mail.crypto.smime.verify` and `verifyAll` with `trustAnchorCertsPem` matched a certificate's issuer to the next certificate's subject by the text node prints, so an intermediate that named its anchor in different case or spacing was refused with `mail-crypto/smime/untrusted-chain`. Names now compare under X.509 name comparison.

items.title: Smaller fixes
items.body: The `finalize` method of a `b.acme.create` client throws `acme/bad-csr` for bytes that are not a parseable PKCS#10 CSR and sends nothing to the CA. `b.privacyPass.buildChallenge` reads `tokenKey` by token type: a SubjectPublicKeyInfo for type `0x0002` and a 49-byte compressed P-384 element for type `0x0001`, throwing `privacy-pass/bad-key` when it does not decode. `b.ai.modelManifest.verify` and `gpai.verifyAdherence` return `reason: "envelope-shape"` for a BOM canonical JSON cannot represent instead of throwing. `b.a2a.verifyCard`, `b.ai.modelManifest.verify`, `gpai.verifyAdherence` and `b.auditSign.verify` accept a valid key given as a Buffer PEM or `{ key: pem }` and do not throw on an unreadable trailing PEM block. `b.pqcAgent` `agent.reloadCerts({ cert, key, ca })` with a new `ca` checks server chains against that `ca`. `b.mtlsEngine.canVerifyInTls` runs the chain check on its probe client and answers `true` only when both sides accept; on Node 24.21.0 and 26.9 the answers for ML-DSA-87, ML-DSA-65 and ECDSA-P384-SHA384 are unchanged.

items.title: Vendored `@blamejs/pki` 0.9.7 and the 2026-10-22 public suffix list
items.body: `@blamejs/pki` moves from 0.9.5 to 0.9.7, which adds the compromised-key list and `pki.x509.sign` refusing a compromised subject or issuer key with `x509/compromised-key`. The first check of a key on each of P-256, P-384, P-521 and secp256k1 in a process builds a table of 255 points for that curve; for P-384 it takes about 110 to 150 ms. The first `b.network.tls.useSystemTrust(true)` call in a process checks every system root; with 145 system roots it took about 1.5 to 1.8 seconds when no key had been checked earlier in the process, and about 0.6 seconds after. The public suffix list is the 2026-10-22_08-36-41_UTC edition.

items.title: DNS over HTTPS uses its own agent
items.body: `b.network.dns` and `b.network.dns.resolver` send DoH queries through a dedicated keep-alive agent that runs the chain check on every new connection. Settings on `https.globalAgent.options`, for example `rejectUnauthorized: false`, no longer apply to DoH queries.

items.title: A compromised certificate is reported ahead of an expired one
items.body: `b.mail.crypto.smime.verify` and `verifyAll` with `trustAnchorCertsPem` throw `mail-crypto/smime/compromised-key` when the path runs through a compromised certificate, even when a certificate in the envelope is expired or not yet valid (they threw `cert-expired` or `cert-not-yet-valid`). `b.mail.bimi.fetchAndVerifyMark` throws `bimi/compromised-key` for a compromised certificate above an expired one (it threw `bimi/vmc-chain-invalid`). `b.tsa.verifyToken` throws `tsa/compromised-key` for a compromised signer certificate that also lacks the timestamping EKU, and for an expired signer or chain certificate under a compromised anchor; a signer certificate whose key cannot be checked throws `tsa/compromised-key` with the message `could not be checked for a compromised key`. `b.mdoc.verifyIssuerSigned` throws `mdoc/compromised-key` for a compromised MSO `deviceKey`, and for an expired document-signer or chain certificate under a compromised IACA.

items.title: New primitives and options
items.body: `b.crypto.compromisedKey(key)`, `b.crypto.assertNotCompromised(key, opts?)`, `b.network.tls.checkClientChains(server)`, `resign(previousPublicKeyPem)` on `b.configDrift` detectors and `resign(previousPublicKey)` on `b.agent.snapshot` handles, `opts.compromisedCode` on `b.crypto.importPublicJwk`, and `opts.requireFile` on `b.atomicFile.fdSafeReadSync`, which refuses anything but a regular file with kind `not-file`, judged on the open descriptor and opened non-blocking. New error codes: `tls/server-chain-unverifiable`, `tls/client-chain-unverifiable`, `tls/resumed-chain-unverifiable`, `config-drift/not-resignable`, `agent-snapshot/signer-key-unreadable`, `agent-snapshot/bad-previous-key`, `agent-snapshot/plaintext-refused` and a `compromised-key` code in each module listed under Security.

items.title: List client-certificate intermediates in the listener's `ca`
items.body: A `requestCert` listener checks each client chain against its `ca`. On Node 24 a listener sees only the client's leaf certificate, so a client certificate issued by an intermediate that the listener's `ca` does not list is refused with `tls/client-chain-unverifiable` (reason `client-chain-unverifiable` in `requireMtls` and `requireBoundKey`). Add the issuing intermediates to `ca`. Node 26 shows the chain the client sent. A listener that serves its client CA from an `SNICallback` context or a `pfx` checks each certificate Node shows when the chain reaches no anchor in `server.ca`; on Node 24 that is only the leaf, so list the client CA certificates in the server's own `ca` to have the intermediates checked.

items.title: Re-sign baselines and snapshots after rotating the audit signing key
items.body: After `b.auditSign.rotateSigningKey()`, an existing `b.configDrift` sidecar is reported as tampered (`signer-untrusted`) and `b.agent.snapshot` rows persisted under the previous key throw `agent-snapshot/bad-signature`. Pass the `previousPublicKey` the rotation returned to `detector.resign(previousPublicKeyPem)` and `snapshot.resign(previousPublicKey)`. `detector.resign` returns `{ resigned: true, capturedAt }`, or `{ resigned: false, reason }` with `already-current` or `no-sidecar`. `snapshot.resign` returns `{ resigned, current, refused }`. A handle with an operator `signer` that reports its key works the same way after that signer's key changes: call `resign(previousPublicKey)` with the key the signer used before. Do not resign when the previous key may have been exposed: neither check detects a baseline or snapshot re-signed by someone who holds the live private key.

items.title: Load or re-seal plaintext agent snapshots
items.body: `b.agent.snapshot` `loadLatest` and `loadById` refuse a row with no sealed wrapper with `agent-snapshot/plaintext-refused`. Set `allowPlaintext: true` to read such rows, or re-seal them. An operator `signer` must return `null` or a public key `b.crypto.compromisedKey` reads from `getPublicKey()`; an opaque identifier such as a KMS key name is refused at `persist`, `loadLatest`, `loadById` and `resign`. Have such a signer return `null` from `getPublicKey()` to keep loading rows through its own `verify`.

items.title: Servers must send a chain that leads to a trust anchor
items.body: A server whose chain puts an expired or unrelated certificate ahead of the issuer that leads to a trust anchor is refused with `tls/server-chain-unverifiable`, even when every key is ordinary. Fix the order of the server's chain. A `checkServerIdentity` built by the framework, including `b.crypto.spkiPinVerifier`, called outside a TLS dial with a certificate that reaches no anchor is refused the same way.

items.title: Use a framework agent to keep `b.httpClient` connections
items.body: An `opts.agent` built as `new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true })` without its own `checkServerIdentity` gets the chain check on each request, and Node opens a new connection for each one. An agent that sets its own `checkServerIdentity` keeps its connections, and that option is replaced with one that runs the chain check first, which also applies to requests made through the agent outside `b.httpClient`. Agents from `b.pqcAgent.create` or `new https.Agent(b.network.tls.applyToContext({ base, role: "client" }))` keep their connections.

items.title: DNS over HTTPS ignores `https.globalAgent.options`
items.body: Move any DoH TLS setting from `https.globalAgent.options` to the `ca` option of `b.network.dns.useDnsOverHttps`.

items.title: Replace DKIM keys of the wrong type and small ARC sealer keys
items.body: A DKIM selector whose key type does not match the `a=` algorithm now fails verification. Publish an RSA key for `rsa-sha256` and an Ed25519 key for `ed25519-sha256`. An ARC sealer key under 2048 bits fails with `too small`; replace it.

items.title: Update rules that read changed audit actions and error codes
items.body: The OpenID Federation chain audit action is `auth.openid_federation.chain_built`. Code that matches errors should read `auth-openid-federation/fetch-failed` and `auth-openid-federation/empty-response` from the federation fetcher, `auth-jwt-external/jwks-fetch-failed` from a JWKS fetch, `tsa/compromised-key` for a TSA signer whose key cannot be checked (it was `crypto/bad-key`), and `mail-crypto/pgp/bad-opts` and `mail-crypto/smime/bad-opts` for an unknown option.

items.title: Replace compromised keys
items.body: A deployment that signs, verifies or trusts with a listed key or a tiny-scalar EC key now fails where it used to work. Run `b.crypto.compromisedKey` over the keys and certificates in configuration to find them before upgrading, and replace each with a freshly generated key. An attestation, token or message signed by such a key cannot be accepted again.

items.title: Outbound TLS constructions run the chain check
items.body: Every place the framework builds outbound TLS options must install the compromised-key chain check as `checkServerIdentity`; a construction that leaves it out fails `codebase-patterns`.

items.title: Certificates are built through one reader
items.body: Every `X509Certificate` the framework builds outside `lib/crypto.js` must come from `bCrypto._x509`, which reads DER bytes as DER; a bare `new X509Certificate(...)` in another file fails `codebase-patterns`.
